This is a list of the **best-selling albums by year in the United States**, published by American music magazine *[Billboard](Billboard_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")* since 1956 as year-end rankings of album sales. For instance, during the 1960s and 1970s, the number-one album as determined by these two publications differed in 10 out of 20 years. From 1992 onwards, the *Billboard* year-end and weekly charts were calculated by [Nielsen SoundScan](Nielsen_SoundScan "Nielsen SoundScan"). Note that this slightly differs from prior *Billboard* year-end album charts, which were a measure of chart performances over twelve months from around December to November (cutoff determined by *Billboard*´s publication schedule) rather than actual total sales.

American singer [Michael Jackson](Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson")'s 1982 *[Thriller](Thriller_(Michael_Jackson_album) "Thriller (Michael Jackson album)")* became the best-selling record in the country for two consecutive years in the 1980s. ***Fearless*** is the second studio [album](Album "Album") by American singer-songwriter [Taylor Swift](Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift"). Under [Big Machine Records](Big_Machine_Records "Big Machine Records") imprint, it was released in the U.S. and Canada on November 11, 2008, and elsewhere on March 9, 2009. Written largely by Swift while she was promoting her [2006 self-titled debut album](Taylor_Swift_(album) "Taylor Swift (album)") in 2007–2008, *Fearless* features additional songwriting credits from [Liz Rose](Liz_Rose "Liz Rose"), [Hillary Lindsey](Hillary_Lindsey "Hillary Lindsey"), [Colbie Caillat](Colbie_Caillat "Colbie Caillat"), and [John Rich](John_Rich "John Rich"). Swift wrote seven of the standard edition's 13 tracks by herself and, in her debut as a [record producer](Record_producer "Record producer"), co-produced the album with [Nathan Chapman](Nathan_Chapman_(record_producer) "Nathan Chapman (record producer)").

*Fearless* is a [country pop](Country_pop "Country pop") album whose composition incorporates country-associated instruments such as [banjos](Banjo "Banjo"), [fiddles](Fiddle "Fiddle"), [mandolins](Mandolin "Mandolin"), and [acoustic guitars](Acoustic_guitar "Acoustic guitar"), that intertwine with dynamic [electric guitars](Electric_guitar "Electric guitar") and [strings](String_instrument "String instrument"). [Music critics](Music_journalism "Music journalism") found the album to feature a [crossover](Crossover_music "Crossover music") appeal brought by the influences of different styles of [pop](Pop_music "Pop music"), [folk](Folk_music "Folk music"), and [rock](Rock_music "Rock music"). Inspired by Swift's teenage feelings, the lyrics explore themes of romance, heartache, and aspirations. The album's title refers to the overarching theme of all of its tracks, as they altogether depict Swift's courage to embrace the challenges of love.

After the release of *Fearless*, Swift embarked on the [Fearless Tour](Fearless_Tour "Fearless Tour"), which ran from April 2009 to July 2010. The album was supported by five [singles](Single_(music) "Single (music)"), including "[Love Story](Love_Story_(Taylor_Swift_song) "Love Story (Taylor Swift song)")" and "[You Belong with Me](You_Belong_with_Me "You Belong with Me")", which performed well and set records on both [country](Country_radio "Country radio") and [pop radio](Pop_radio "Pop radio"). In the U.S., *Fearless* spent 11 weeks atop the [*Billboard* 200](Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") and was [certified Diamond](RIAA_certification "RIAA certification") by the [Recording Industry Association of America](Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA). It peaked in the top five of albums charts and received [multi-platinum certifications](List_of_music_recording_certifications "List of music recording certifications") in Australia, Canada, New Zealand, and the U.K., and has sold 12 million copies worldwide.

***Red*** is the fourth studio album by American singer-songwriter [Taylor Swift](Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift"). Inspired by the fantasy series *[Game of Thrones](Game_of_Thrones "Game of Thrones")*, she split the album's lyrical scope in two: one is about the downsides of fame and the resultant anger, and the other about love amidst the tumult.
